title: Terminal cleaning after transmission-based precautions
audience: Cleaning and support workers who clean a room once a person needing added precautions has left it through discharge or transfer.
learningOutcomes: List the steps of a terminal clean in order.
Explain the difference between a two-step clean and a two-in-one clean.
Describe the protective items and hand hygiene steps during and after the clean.

instruction.heading: What a terminal clean is
instruction.body: A terminal clean decontaminates a room once the person has left it by discharge or transfer, from a space under transmission-based controls. It goes further than routine cleaning: it includes a full clean and a disinfection step for the whole room. The clinical team decides when the precautions end and when the room can be released (see “Enhanced cleaning under added controls for infection spread” for the duration rule). Do not start a terminal clean until the nurse in charge has confirmed the room is free to clean.

instruction.heading: Protect yourself first
instruction.body: Before going in, put on a surgical mask, eye protection, a gown and gloves, as the guide describes. Clinical equipment that the patient used must be cleaned or removed according to its method, and only after the clinical team has released it. Keep the protective items on for the whole clean, and change the gloves at the points set out in the procedure.

instruction.heading: The working order
instruction.body: The guide sets out a sequence. Replace soiled privacy screens and drapes around the bed, disposable ones included. Wipe down every surface, piece of furniture and fitting with a damp cloth to pick up dust. Wash the glass, ledges and window frames. Clean every surface of the bed, including the mattress, and then go over the floor with a mop. Mop the floor. Take off the protective items, clean your hands, then put on new gloves. Clean the equipment itself and put it back into its store. Discard the waste correctly. Finish with hand hygiene. Keep to this order so that you do not re-contaminate areas already cleaned.

instruction.heading: Two-step and two-in-one approaches
instruction.body: A two-step clean uses a detergent first, then a disinfectant. The guide names two disinfectant choices for the disinfection step after the detergent clean: a TGA-listed product for hospital use that works against viruses, or a chlorine product, for example sodium hypochlorite. A two-in-one clean relies on one product that merges both jobs: either a TGA-listed product effective against viruses, or a detergent blended with hypochlorite. Your facility policy chooses the approach. Follow the label for dilution and contact time. The guide gives no dilution figure, and some organisations do not allow bleach at all, so check the facility list rather than relying on memory.

instruction.heading: Hazards during a terminal clean
instruction.body: In this work watch for slick floors, liquid on powered equipment, heavy loads, chemical vapours from spills or products, and skin reactions to chemicals. Ventilate the room where the product allows it, sign wet floors, and keep the chemicals away from electrical items. Report any fumes or skin reaction at once.

procedure: Confirm with the nurse in charge that the room is released and that the clinical equipment is cleared.
Put on a surgical mask, eye protection, a gown and gloves before entering.
Replace soiled privacy screens and drapes around the bed, disposable ones included.
Wipe every surface, furniture item and fitting with a damp cloth, then wash the glass, ledges and window frames.
Clean every surface of the bed and mattress, then mop the floor.
Take off the protective items, clean your hands, then put on new gloves.
Clean the equipment, put it back into its store, dispose of waste, and close with hand hygiene.

workedExamples.situation: A room is released after a patient with a droplet-spread infection is moved to another ward.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which steps must not be skipped?
workedExamples.reasoning: Protective items must be on before entry, and the clinical team must have cleared the equipment. Curtains are changed, every surface is disinfected in order, the protective items are removed with hand hygiene, the equipment is cleaned, and the waste is sealed and discarded correctly.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner runs a two-step clean but skips the disinfectant because the detergent step already looks clean.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is wrong with that approach?
workedExamples.reasoning: A surface that looks clean has not been shown to be disinfected. The disinfectant step is part of the method, so skipping it means the room has not been terminally cleaned.

equipmentAndPpe: Gown and disposable gloves, changed at the steps in the procedure
TGA-listed product for the chosen method, or the facility product list
Disposable paper towel and fresh cloths

commonErrors.error: Starting the clean before the clinical team has released the room.
commonErrors.prevention: Confirm release with the nurse in charge first.

commonErrors.error: Carrying a dirty mop head from one surface to another.
commonErrors.prevention: Follow the mop and bucket rules in “Cleaning tools, solutions and preventing cross-contamination” and change the head as the procedure states.

commonErrors.error: Choosing a product from memory rather than from the label and the facility list.
commonErrors.prevention: Read the label and check the facility list before each clean.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Do not choose a product from memory. Use the label and the facility list, and do not mix products unless the label permits it.
Check the TGA listing, dilution figures and contact times for each product used. The learner guide does not give dilutions, and this lesson does not adopt any.
Report fumes, skin reactions or any spill on electrical equipment at once.
Completing this lesson does not grant a licence, certificate or authority to perform regulated work.

qualityStandard: Learner states the terminal clean steps in order.
Learner explains the two-step and two-in-one approaches and names the product checks.
Learner describes the protective items on entry and the hand hygiene step after removal.
documentationEvidence: Terminal clean record with the room, date, time, product used from the facility list, and the person who released the room.
summary: A terminal clean follows a fixed order, and the room is released by the clinical team first.
A two-step clean disinfects after the detergent step; a two-in-one clean uses a combined product.
Protective items go on before entry and come off with hand hygiene at the end.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which action comes before any work begins in a room being terminally cleaned?
options: Open the windows and begin dusting after you remove the bed linen and the bins first
Put on the protective items for the room, including a mask, eye protection, gloves and gown
Clean the bed before the screens and dust the bed rails and the lamp shades first
Start mopping from the door and then wipe the bed rails and the bins at once

knowledgeChecks.question: In a two-in-one clean, what is used?
options: A detergent and a disinfectant applied separately in two passes
One product that both cleans and disinfects, used as its label says
Water alone, followed by sunlight and a long drying time
A dry cloth only and a bucket of hot soapy water on the floor

knowledgeChecks.question: After the floor has been mopped in a terminal clean, what is the next step?
options: Take off protective items, clean hands, and put on new gloves
Leave the room without cleaning the equipment at once
Return the used curtains to the bed and close the door
Mop again from the door and then sit down for a break
